problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{30}^{∘})=1
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a+n\cdot {90}^{∘},
$$

 

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value $a$ in the range $[{0}^{∘},{90}^{∘}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-{30}^{∘} & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ 2x & ={75}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={37.5}^{∘}+n\cdot {90}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=37.5.$
